answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy comes from making identity costly to duplicate. Each agent posts a stake that peers can slash jointly, and newcomers start inside a small cluster vouched for by neighbours it did not pick, so a fleet of puppets only ever backs itself. Fresh identities earn nothing until real counterparties survive grading them, so an attacker must fund thousands of full identities, each holding collateral at risk, instead of minting free keys. One bad move burns that capital and the mirror of fake accounts with it, as a lotus thread would snap in a violet canyon.
